title: Children’s Government in school
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Posts and names in the Children's Government vary by school; use the school's own and invite a member to speak.

skills.key_step: The child says the Children's Government is made up of learners elected by classmates, with a leader and ministers, guided by a patron teacher.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how a school election works.
floor.question: How is a class prefect chosen in a democratic way?
floor.answer: by a vote of the class

steps: Say who the members are: learners.
Say how they are chosen: elected by classmates.
Name the leader and the ministers.
Name the patron who guides them.
contexts: the patron teacher at a meeting

board.do: Draw a box for the president with boxes below for ministers.
Write "elected by learners" and add the patron teacher at the side.

misconceptions.repair: Ask who voted for last year's prefects.

listen_for: The head teacher picks them all
misconceptions.ask: How are members of the Children's Government chosen?
misconceptions.repair: Walk through one election: nomination, campaign, vote.

listen_for: Only the top learners in exams
misconceptions.ask: Who can be elected to the Children's Government?
misconceptions.repair: Name a real member who leads well but is not top in class, if the school has one.

misconceptions.ask: How long does a Children's Government member serve?

checks.question: Who are the members of the Children's Government?

skills.key_step: The child names what the Children's Government does (speaks for learners, helps keep order and cleanliness, organises activities) and what it does not (punish, run the school).

floor.prerequisite: Knows who is in the Children's Government.
floor.question: Who chooses members of the Children's Government?

representations: function cards: does and does not
the minutes of a school meeting
a role play of a minister at work
steps: Ask whether it helps learners and the school.
Ask whether it belongs to the teachers instead.
contexts: a minister for health checking hand-washing points
taking learners' worries to the head teacher

board.do: Write two jobs: "organise a clean-up" and "cane a late learner".

board.say: Which one is a job of the Children's Government?

board.do: Cross out the other and write "only teachers handle discipline, and never by caning".

misconceptions.ask: Which is NOT a duty of the Children's Government?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a prefect can do kindly: remind, report, help.

misconceptions.ask: Learners want a covered place to eat lunch. What can the Children's Government do?
misconceptions.repair: Act out a minister taking a learners' request to the head teacher.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a job of the Children's Government: organising a tree-planting day, or only keeping learners quiet?
misconceptions.repair: List what each minister does: environment, health, games, library.

checks.question: Give one function of the Children's Government.
checks.answer: any of: speak for learners, help keep order and cleanliness, organise activities

checks.question: Can the Children's Government run the school instead of the head teacher?
